{"id": "q85", "type": "why", "claims": ["c1", "c2"], "pair": null, "question": "Why is the rule c_{n,i} > c_{n,u} in Eq. 1 equivalent to including a node whenever c_{n,i} exceeds 0.5, and what condition must hold for that equivalence?", "answer": "If the two coefficients sum to one, then c_{n,u} = 1 − c_{n,i}. {"id": "q86", "type": "why", "claims": ["c1", "c7"], "pair": null, "question": "Why does S³martCirc need the full model's output distribution for the training prompts in all six configurations listed in Appendix A?", "answer": "Every configuration uses alpha of 0.25 or 0.75, which is never zero. {"id": "q89", "type": "why", "claims": ["c3", "c6"], "pair": null, "question": "Why does the Acronym generator keep a word only if its formatted version's first token is the space-prefixed capital letter?", "answer": "The task requires the model to retrieve a word's capital letter and output it; the reference circuit uses letter mover heads for this step. {"id": "q90", "type": "why", "claims": ["c3", "c4"], "pair": null, "question": "What does Act.'s −100.00% Acc. on Qwen Acronym imply about the masked model's accuracy, and why?", "answer": "It implies the model with Act.'s circuit nodes masked answered none of the samples correctly. {"id": "q91", "type": "counterfactual", "claims": ["c1", "c2"], "pair": "p1", "question": "Under Eq. 1, would a node with c_{n,i} = 0.6 and c_{n,u} = 0.4 be selected as a candidate circuit node?", "answer": "Yes. c_{n,i} is the larger of the two coefficients, so the argmax assigns the node to the circuit, before any connectivity pruning.", "rubric": ["Says yes, it is selected.", "Reason: c_i is the argmax of the two coefficients."]},

{"id": "q105", "type": "connect", "claims": ["c1", "c7"], "pair": null, "question": "If Figure 5 had shown that alpha = 0 on GPT-2 IOI yields circuits as good as alpha = 0.75, which argument from the ablation discussion would lose support?", "answer": "The argument that removing the faithfulness term would make the optimization keep only a narrow set of components that boost one token. alpha = 0 is exactly the setting in which the KL faithfulness term is switched off.", "rubric": ["Identifies the RQ4 claim that dropping the faithfulness term harms the circuit (it retains only narrow components that boost one token).", "Links this to alpha = 0 being equivalent to removing the KL term in Eq. 2."]},

{"id": "q12", "type": "failure", "claims": ["c1", "c2", "c7"], "pair": null, "question": "Would S³martCirc's claimed advantage, that each node is evaluated in the context of all others, still hold if the regularizer drove the coefficients to near-binary values very early in training, before L_disc had shaped them?", "answer": "Largely not. {"id": "q161", "type": "why", "claims": ["c3", "c1"], "pair": null, "question": "Why does the Acronym prompt template end with '(AB', and which token serves as y in Eq. 2's correctness term for this task?", "answer": "The task is to predict the last letter of a three-letter acronym. {"id": "q162", "type": "why", "claims": ["c3", "c4"], "pair": null, "question": "Why does swapping the second name give the patching baselines a useful corrupted counterpart for IOI?", "answer": "In 'When N1 and N2 went to the PLACE, N1 handed the OBJECT to', N1 is the repeated subject and N2 is the indirect object, which is the answer. {"id": "q165", "type": "counterfactual", "claims": ["c2"], "pair": "p_conf_abs", "question": "For a coefficient that has drifted to v = 1.2, does the confidence term ½|v(1−v)| push it back toward 1?", "answer": "Yes. ANSWER Q5: Acc. is a percentage change in discrete answer accuracy, while Logit. is a normalized continuous logit change. A normalized logit shift of −1.00 can cross the decision boundary on every example and therefore correspond to a −100% accuracy change.

ANSWER Q6: The randomly selected nodes generally do not form an input-to-output connected causal path. After the connectivity handling used in evaluation, they have no effective intervention on the output, so every run gives exactly zero accuracy change despite selecting many nodes.

ANSWER Q8: No meaningful change would be expected in the reported configuration. Its 60 warmup epochs already occupy the entire 60-epoch run, so the alpha-weighted post-warmup objective does not get an opportunity to shape the circuit.

ANSWER Q11: It would illustrate the RQ2 caveat that behavioral impact and recovery of a reference circuit need not agree.
